issues.legal_issue: Children deemed legitimate because they were born from a void marriage do not thereby acquire rights in property belonging to persons other than their parents.
material_facts: The children were born from a marriage that was void because an earlier marriage was still subsisting.
They claimed shares in ancestral coparcenary property shared with persons other than their parents.
The courts below denied the children shares in that coparcenary property, and they appealed that decision.
issues.conclusion: The children could not claim shares in the coparcenary property under Section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act; their statutory rights were confined to the property of their parents. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(1) and (2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, as amended by the Marriage Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976, deem children of a void or annulled marriage legitimate. But Section 16(3), which applies notwithstanding those subsections, expressly prevents that status from conferring rights in the property of anyone other than the parents where the children would otherwise have been incapable of acquiring those rights because they were not legitimate. The protective purpose of Section 16 cannot be used to extend rights beyond the statutory limit. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.appeal_against_denial: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decision that denied children a claimed share in property.
predicates.children_from_void_marriage: The children were born from a marriage that was void.
predicates.claim_to_property_of_nonparents: The children claimed rights in property belonging, at least in part, to persons other than their parents.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the denial of a property claim by children born from a void marriage, and the claim concerns property belonging to persons other than their parents, the children have no right to that property.
